External / portable drive · Clicking or grinding noises

External Hard Drive Clicking, Grinding or Beeping

Clicking, grinding or beeping from the drive inside usually means the read/write heads (the tiny arms that read the disk) or the motor are failing. Each time you power it on, the damage can grow, and portable drives are easily hurt by drops.

5/5 · Pro territory
Success odds: Low

Mechanical faults worsen with every power-up, and real repairs need a cleanroom.

✋ Stop! Don't do this first

  • Unplug it and leave it off. Do not keep trying, because each power-up can scratch the disk inside.
  • Do not use the freezer trick, tap it or shake it. These are myths that can do harm.
  • Never open the drive itself. Dust ruins the disk, and it needs a cleanroom.
  • Do not run recovery scans, CHKDSK or any repair tool on it. Heavy reading stresses a failing drive, and making a copy (see below) is the only DIY step worth trying.

Your steps

0 of 7 done
  1. Show me how
    1. Unplug the USB cable, and the power adapter if there is one.
    2. Write down what you heard: clicking, grinding, beeping or nothing, and when it started.
  2. Show me how
    1. Irreplaceable files such as family photos: skip to the last step and contact a professional.
    2. Replaceable files or you accept the risk: read on, and plan for one careful try at most.

    Guide: How to find a trustworthy data recovery professional

  3. Show me how
    1. Do not remove the drive from its case.
    2. Do not move it to another case either.
  4. Show me how
    1. Use one good, short USB cable. If the drive has its own power adapter or a Y-cable (a cable with two USB plugs), use it.
    2. Plug into a USB port directly on the computer.
    3. If it spins and appears, go straight to making an image. If it clicks again, unplug.
  5. Show me how
    1. Boot a Linux live USB (a USB stick that runs its own system without installing anything) on a computer, press Ctrl+Alt+T to open a terminal and type sudo apt install gddrescue. Then plug in the healthy destination drive and open it in the Files app, and only then plug in the clicking drive.
    2. In the terminal run lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,MODEL to see both drives by size. Note the name of each, such as sdb and sdc.
    3. Run sudo ddrescue -n /dev/sdX /media/ubuntu/DEST/drive.img /media/ubuntu/DEST/drive.map, where sdX is the clicking drive and DEST is the destination drive's name (Linux Mint: /media/mint/DEST). Run only this first pass; skip the retry pass. Always type the failing drive first and the empty destination second. If you swap them, the copy erases your data.

    Guide: How to make an image (exact copy) of a driveGuide: How to make a Linux live USB (step by step)

  6. Show me how
    1. Power off and unplug the clicking drive.
    2. Run TestDisk on the image to list folders, then PhotoRec if names are lost.
    3. Save recovered files to a third drive.

    Guide: How to use TestDisk to copy files off a driveGuide: How to use PhotoRec to recover photos and files

  7. Show me how
    1. Power off at the first stall or click.
    2. Pack the drive in a padded box and ask a few labs for a price and their policy if they cannot recover anything.

    Guide: How to find a trustworthy data recovery professional

Mission complete! 🎉 Check your recovered files open properly, then back them up in two places.

Tools you'll use

GNU ddrescue

Copies a failing drive to an image file, retrying bad areas so you work from a copy, not the original.

  • Linux · macOS
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

HDDSuperClone

Linux tool for cloning a failing drive sector by sector, with options that skip and retry bad areas.

  • Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

ddrescueview

Free graphical viewer that shows which parts of a ddrescue image are good, bad or still unread.

  • Windows · Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

smartmontools

Free open-source suite that reads S.M.A.R.T. health data from drives to show early signs of failure.

  • Windows · macOS · Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

TestDisk

Free open-source tool that finds lost partitions and repairs boot sectors so files can be read again.

  • Windows · macOS · Linux
  • Free (open source)

WebsiteDocs

PhotoRec

Free open-source file carver that recovers files by signature, even when the file system is damaged.

  • Windows · macOS · Linux
  • Free (open source)

If it clicks, grinds, beeps or will not spin and the data matters, stop and ask a professional with a cleanroom.

Questions people ask

Is clicking caused by the USB case?

Usually no. The sound comes from the drive's moving parts. A weak power supply can trigger it on some portables, so trying a better power source once is reasonable.

Can I put it in the freezer?

No. It is a myth that can cause water damage from condensation. Experts advise against it.

Can I swap it into another case?

It will not fix a mechanical fault, and some drives have soldered USB or encryption tied to the original board. Avoid it unless you know the exact model.
